questions.text: Convert the pre-fix expression to in-fix [latex]-^{*}+A B C^{*}-D E+F G[/latex]
questions.solution:
Read the prefix expression from the right, pushing operands; on an operator, pop two and combine as (first operator second):
- + F G [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (F+G)
- [latex]-[/latex] D E [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (D[latex]-[/latex]E), then * [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ((D[latex]-[/latex]E)*(F+G))
- + A B [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (A+B), then * C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ((A+B)*C)
- the leading [latex]-[/latex] joins the two halves

Result: (((A+B)*C)[latex]-[/latex]((D[latex]-[/latex]E)*(F+G)))

Answer: (((A+B)*C)-((D-E)*(F+G)))

Originally all Options are wrong. We have modified one option.

questions.text: Consider the array representation of a binary min-heap containing 1023 elements. The minimum number of comparisons required to find the maximum in the heap is ___________.
questions.solution:
In a min-heap the maximum is always at a leaf. With 1023 nodes there are [latex]\lceil1023/2\rceil=512[/latex] leaves.

Finding the maximum of 512 elements needs 512 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 511 comparisons.

Answer: 511

questions.text: In a balanced binary search tree with n elements, what is the worst case time complexity of reporting all elements in range [a,b]? Assume that the number of reported elements is k.
questions.solution:
Search for a in [latex]O(\log n)[/latex] (tree height), then do an in-order walk reporting elements until passing b. The walk visits the k answers plus [latex]O(\log n)[/latex] boundary nodes.

Total [latex]\Theta(\log n+k)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\Theta(\log n+k)[/latex]

questions.text: Consider a double hashing scheme in which the primary hash function is [latex]h_1(k)=k\; mod \; 23[/latex], and the secondary hash function is [latex]h_2(k)=1+(k\; mod \; 19)[/latex]. Assume that the table size is 23. Then the address returned by probe 1 in the probe sequence (assume that the probe sequence begins at probe 0) for key value k=90 is_____________.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]h_1(90)=90\bmod23=21[/latex]
- [latex]h_2(90)=1+(90\bmod19)=1+14=15[/latex]

Probe i = [latex](h_1+i\cdot h_2)\bmod23[/latex]. Probe 1 = [latex](21+15)\bmod23=36\bmod23=13[/latex]

Answer: 13

questions.text: What is the worst case time complexity of inserting n elements into an empty linked list, if the linked list needs to be maintained in sorted order?
questions.solution:
To keep the list sorted, each insertion must first find its position by walking the list: up to k steps when the list has k elements.

Total in the worst case: [latex]1+2+\cdots+(n-1)=\Theta(n^2)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex]
